articles.summary: Meta has launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its first frontier AI models designed for complex tasks and long-term memory.

These larger systems improve upon the earlier lightweight Muse Spark, delivering stronger coding capabilities and benchmark results on par with Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. Aiming to build persistent personal assistants, Meta designed the models with an active memory feature to retain and synthesize user information over long periods

articles.title: Elon Musk Bragged About His Grok Lego Star Wars Haul. Then X Users Punked Him
articles.summary: Elon Musk accidentally exposed his private purchase details on X, allowing users to tamper with his Grok-assisted Lego Star Wars order.
articles.paragraph: While showcasing his Grok AI tool on X, Elon Musk accidentally revealed his Lego order number, email, and partial payment details to over 240 million followers. Pranksters swiftly capitalized on the leak, with an account named Enderman attempting to cancel the Star Wars purchase through Lego's customer service chatbot. Musk claimed the order survived, but another user manipulated Lego's AI assistant to switch the delivery address and increase the order to 400 sets on Musk's card. Lego declined to comment on whether its automated systems or human staff flagged the suspicious changes. The mishap occurred just after Musk, Meta, and OpenAI pushed the benefits of using AI agents for automated shopping tasks. However, Visa recently warned that fraudulent sellers are tricking shopping bots to steal sensitive payment information. Highlighting the vulnerability, Visa recorded a 40 percent spike in malicious bot-driven transactions across the United States in late 2025.

articles.title: The US Army is handing out over $4.15 billion to any company able to stop low-cost drone attacks on home soil
articles.summary: US Army awards $4.15 billion to 10 companies to defend bases against cheap drones after Iranian attacks damaged American facilities.
articles.paragraph: US Army launches $4.15B counter-drone marketplace with 10 companies — but relies on strict open architecture to break vendor lock-in The awards fall under Domestic Shield, a Department of Defense initiative intended to strengthen protection against unmanned aircraft without restricting procurement to individual suppliers. Seven companies will receive $500 million each, while three others secured smaller awards, establishing a multi-vendor arrangement with a maximum value of $7 billion. Allen Control Systems, Digital Force Technologies, DroneShield, L3Harris WESCAM, Napatree Technology, RADA Technologies and SRC each received contracts with $500 million base values under the initiative.

articles.title: Valor Mortis review: even with satisfying parry-focused combat, it's impossible to overlook flaws
articles.summary: Valor Mortis offers a satisfying and meaty parry-focused combat system at its core while showing flashes of inventiveness in some areas and set pieces, but several frustrating elements keep rearing up...
articles.paragraph: Valor Mortis offers a satisfying and meaty parry-focused combat system at its core while showing flashes of inventiveness in some areas and set pieces, but several frustrating elements keep rearing up that prevent it from landing entirely. The snappy and satisfying parry-focused combat of Valor Mortis will surely delight fans of Sekiro and Lies of P who are looking for a ‘Souls-like’ experience from a new perspective. But while it builds on that core with some inventive set pieces and a gloomy atmosphere, the restrictions of the first-person view make some encounters clunky or irritating, and an obsession with trickery is grating. articles.title: The Apple Upgrade program is great for consumers and Apple, but bad for carriers like Verizon and AT&T — here's why
articles.summary: The original iPhone transformed the way carriers like AT&T operate — and the Apple Upgrade program is Apple's next big power play.
articles.paragraph: The original iPhone transformed the way carriers like AT&T operate — and the Apple Upgrade program is Apple The same existential threat applied to all carriers except AT&T and O2, which had exclusive launch rights to the iPhone in the US and UK, respectively. Fast-forward 19 years, and Apple has repeatedly proven that the iPhone's popularity gives it considerable power over its carrier partners — customers are no longer loyal to the carrier providing the mobile service, but to the brand behind their favorite phone. Apple's newest commercial venture, the Apple Upgrade program — which was announced earlier this year and is, at the time of writing, still only available in the US — is the latest dagger to the heart of major MNOs (Mobile Network Operators).

articles.paragraph: A northern gannet scans the sea for fish from 100 feet (30 meters) in the air. Upon seeing a school, it pitches its body into a nosedive, somehow breaking the surface at 70 miles per hour (113 kilometers per hour) without breaking its neck. This daring maneuver seems to defy the laws of nature, but it's standard hunting behavior for plunge-diving seabirds.

articles.title: From GTA V on iPhone to Free Photoshop: This AI Tool Is Upending Software
articles.summary: REA, a free toolkit that hands AI agents the keys to reverse engineering, crossed 100,000 GitHub stars in a week as AI-decompiled game mods, console ports, and Adobe clones flood the internet.
articles.paragraph: REA, a free toolkit that hands AI agents the keys to reverse engineering, is the hottest thing on Github right now. Here's why. Would you like to kill a boss in Skyrim using an AK47 from Counter Strike? Give your NPCs a real genius-level brain that gives you unique answers instead of predefined strings of text? Would you like to run GTA V on your iPhone? What about using paid software for free, and legally? Well, people are doing that and more with AI right now. A free tool that lets AI agents pull apart almost any piece of software has become the hottest project on GitHub, jumping from fewer than 10,000 stars on October 6 to more than 100,000 by Monday. It’s called REA, short for Reverse Engineer Anything.
